source_caption: Aaron Paul walked the Kloz Horse Fall/Winter 2004 runway in New York, four years before he became a household name as Jesse Pinkman in Breaking Bad. Wearing loose denim, distressed layers, and a deliberately worn-in silhouette, his look embodied the raw, anti-fashion aesthetic that defined much of the early 2000s. Midway through the show, he lit a cigarette, turning the runway into something that felt more like a character performance than a traditional fashion presentation. Looking back, it’s striking how closely this forgotten appearance mirrors the rebellious persona that would later make him famous. One of fashion’s most unexpected and overlooked pop culture moments.
